core.text: Objective boundary inversion: increase the preferred intervention, scheduled refreshes before commits, from three to four and then five refreshes. Insert each additional refresh after the first selection and before its commit. Keep three target selections and three commits, fixed target statuses, row binding and the mismatch-request rule. Extra scheduled refreshes are unconditional dose increments; this does not sever or suppress the mismatch-to-refresh return link. These are proposed diagnostic schedules, not completed corrections.

Declare adversity at the first actual written key different from its intended key, even if later repaired, or when the remaining required actions cannot finish by minute ten. Log times, ordinary and mismatch-triggered refresh counts separately, loaded snapshots, retained rows, intended keys and every write. Stop before an action would exceed the budget. Six indispensable selection/commit actions plus q scheduled and h executed mismatch refreshes require at least 6+q+h minutes; q+h above four is infeasible.

Hypothesis under changing snapshots and row binding: three-refresh dosing already reproduces the initial K2-intended/K5-written mismatch. Adding one or two early refreshes still leaves S1 loaded at the first commit, so it cannot rescue that initial write. Key-bound controls predict correct target writes with no mismatch refreshes: three refreshes cost nine minutes, four cost ten, and five require eleven. Five-refresh controls must stop incomplete by ten. Verify final loaded S2 and exact statuses in any candidate completion.

residue.text: Refresh dose also advances snapshot eligibility; observed differences cannot independently establish a dose effect. Cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding, preserving the dose-specific action schedule across controls. Equal scores for K5 and K7 require key-based detection. All proposed outcomes concern the stipulated model; real binding, detection costs, concurrency and failures remain unknown.

Only the single stipulated wrong-target write is observed. Repeated mismatch feedback, correction success and human benefit remain unestablished. Count return requests without interpreting them as proven recurrence. No production system or participant is available.

tension.account_a: Dose-rescue hypothesis: increasing scheduled refreshes from three to four restores intended-key correction within the budget.
tension.account_b: Identity-and-budget hypothesis: extra refreshes preserve the initial retained-row mismatch; five total refreshes make completion impossible regardless of binding.
tension.prediction_a: At four scheduled refreshes, the first K2-intended commit writes K2 and the complete exact-target correction finishes by minute ten.
tension.prediction_b: At four scheduled refreshes with row binding, the first commit still writes K5; with key binding it writes K2. At five refreshes even the key-bound schedule cannot finish within ten.
